items.reason: A gentle, non-active cleanser keeps the routine simple and leaves room for your actives.
Niacinamide is a gentle first active that suits skin with an oily look and pairs well with a retinol.
A lower-strength retinol is a sensible starting point for a nightly active aimed at smoother-looking skin over time.
A light ceramide moisturizer supports a comfortable skin barrier while your skin gets used to retinol.
Daily mineral SPF 50 is needed alongside retinol, which makes skin more sun-sensitive.

response.routine_note: Mornings: cleanse, niacinamide, moisturizer, then SPF; evenings: cleanse, retinol, then moisturizer, starting retinol just 2 nights a week and building up slowly as your skin allows. If you notice lasting stinging, peeling or irritation, pause the retinol and see a pharmacist or dermatologist.
